_about: Design decisions made from variant boards (design doc: Execution plan > Decision workflow). One record per decision, appended, never rewritten once chosen. Every record is reported to Alex so it can be added to the design doc's decision log, which stays the source of truth; this file is what the build reads.

record_shape.area: the design doc area, e.g. Trees, Shadows, Walls, UI
record_shape.question: what was being decided, in one line
record_shape.board: variants/<id>/ -- the board the choice was made from; its seed and parameter sets are in that folder's board.json
record_shape.chosen: a variant name, 'blend of A and B', or 'new round'
record_shape.status: proposed | chosen by Alex | logged in design doc

decisions.question: How transparent should cast shadows be? (Alex: shadows need to be softer, meaning more transparent)
decisions.chosen: D
decisions.notes: Alex: 'default to D for now'. Open follow-up raised with it: whether shadows should darken as the sun climbs (a sun-elevation coupling); not decided.

decisions.question: The unit art mockup's proposals: side colours, where each side's colour goes, and how far a plane's shadow sits from it
decisions.board: reference/mockups/unit_sheet.html (a mockup sheet, not a variant board)
decisions.chosen: as proposed
decisions.notes: Alex: 'I love the rest of the decisions. The accent colors are perfectly toned. Those might be useful colors to mirror in the HUD.' The pen line was left open (variants/pen-line/).

decisions.question: Should an ink line's width vary along it, and how?
options: C heavier on the shadow side
decisions.chosen: C
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Shadow side looks the best.' Factor values are the board's; tuning them is a later board.

decisions.question: The sandbox demo's baseline: map scale, turn length, steps, stalls, map edge, ready-up, empty plans, the minute of flight
decisions.board: none (a recommendation table in chat; the scale options came from Track T's and Track S's arithmetic)
decisions.chosen: as recommended

parameters.stalls: none in the demo; later a stall may cost an altitude band
parameters.map_edge: the planner refuses a step that ends outside the map; the AI turns back on its own
parameters.ready_up: editing a plan after Ready un-readies that player; the turn plays when the last player is ready
parameters.empty_plan: the plane flies on straight at its current speed
parameters.minute_of_flight: a simulated minute (about 12 turns), which sizes the map at 5,000 m

decisions.notes: Alex: '1-7 look good'. The scale is a starting value: the demo exposes it as a live knob so Alex can decide by flying. Items 8 (how height reads in ink) and 9 (terrain level fills vs object fills) are still open.

decisions.question: How does height read in ink on the full render?
decisions.chosen: B
decisions.notes: Alex: 'I strongly prefer the contours visually but I am not sure what they are signaling.' Open with it: what line breaks mean, and whether height steps are passable to ground units.

decisions.question: How do object fills relate to the ground level they stand on?
options: today: ground +0.025 L per level, fills fixed
1: fills step up with the ground
decisions.chosen: today
decisions.notes: Alex: 'For ground level fill - I actually like the current look the most.' Accepted with it: on the top level, wall and rock fills sit slightly darker than the ground (-0.018 / -0.011 L).

decisions.question: Are height steps passable to ground units, and what do the contours signal?
options: A every step a cliff, crossed at ramps or roads
B every step a slope, crossed anywhere slower
C mixed: some edges cliffs, some slopes
decisions.chosen: A

parameters.rule: every height step is a cliff: impassable to ground units, crossed only at ramps or roads
parameters.contours: tightly packed at every step (a cliff); a gap in the lines marks a ramp
parameters.contour_breaks_now: none: lines drawn unbroken until ramps exist
parameters.ramp_shadows: when ramps are added, their shadows must be complete and correct (a ramp is a sloped surface: its shadow varies along it and meets the cliff's); no partial version

decisions.notes: Alex first chose C (mixed cliffs and slopes), then: 'Actually, I take that back. Lets do A.' Also: 'draw the lines unbroken for now'. Ramps come with roads and ground units. On ramps: 'The shadows are much more complex with ramps. I don't want to do them less then 100% when we add them.'

decisions.notes: Alex: 'go with your fog recommendations'. Asked with it: show line of sight occluded, e.g. a tank's view inside a valley.

decisions.question: What decides what a unit's guns can hit?
options: one forward cone per plane type, plus fire at will / hold fire (proposed)
decisions.chosen: a cone per weapon

parameters.rule: every weapon has its own cone; a bomber's tail turret and its front guns are different weapons with different cones
parameters.target_priority: wanted eventually; not designed or built yet
parameters.hardpoints: every gun sits on a hardpoint, a mount point on the airframe ([forward, right, up] metres from the unit's centre); its cone starts there (Alex, later the same day: 'We will want guns to have hardpoints')

applied_to: nothing yet: the first-fight pass builds it (proposed plan in the design doc)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Let's do a cone per weapon. There's a huge difference between a turret on the back of a bomber and the front guns.' Idea Alex is still thinking through, NOT to design or build yet: a special used on an area pre-aims it, so an enemy revealed there by the fog may be hit with higher accuracy.

decisions.question: How does a weapon's fire resolve into hits?
options: no dice: damage builds inside the cone, falling off with range (proposed)
a random roll per burst from a shared seed
decisions.chosen: random-ish, from a number of factors to be modelled over time

parameters.first_factor: machine guns: better odds the closer the target is to the centre of the cone

applied_to: nothing yet: the first-fight pass builds it (proposed plan in the design doc)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'It should be randomish with a bunch of factors we will want to model later.'

decisions.question: Can guns fire between altitude bands?
options: same band, or one band away with a penalty (proposed)

parameters.rule: a weapon's cone has a vertical extent too; a target above or below is in reach when it is inside the cone, with odds by the same rule as across

applied_to: nothing yet: the first-fight pass builds it (proposed plan in the design doc)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Same cone behavior.'

decisions.question: Hills cannot hide a plane (ground tops out at 24 m, the low air band is 120 m). Make the ground taller?

keep the ground low; hiding is for ground units
decisions.chosen: taller ground: mountainous islands, for tactical options

parameters.deferred: off for now; revisit once there are reasons to (Alex, 2026-10-09)
parameters.alternative: bring the lowest flight band much closer to mountain height instead of (or as well as) raising the ground (Alex)

Later the same day: 'Let's leave mountains off for now. We'll come back and visit them once we have reasons to. decisions.question: How does a special (the bomb today) get its target, and how is its area of effect shown?
decisions.board: none (options in chat: A aim on the step, B a target per step, C a target selection, D target first with the step found for you)
options: A aim on the step (as built)
D target first, the step found for you
decisions.chosen: a target selection: with a friendly unit selected, the player can also select an enemy unit or a point on the map. It shows on the side view, and activating a special on a step takes it: the special is active and targeted FOR THAT STEP, so one unit can carry different targets (and different specials) on different steps. No target, no activation. Non-special weapons need no target: they fire on their own

parameters.target: an enemy unit or a point on the map, selected while a friendly unit is selected
parameters.binding: per step: a special is activated on a step and keeps the target it was given there
effects: the target a special uses when activated on a step
parameters.no_target: the special cannot be activated (Drop is disabled until there is a target)
parameters.set_by: left-click an enemy unit, right-click a point on the map (Alex: fine for now; right-click beside right-drag panning is awkward and will change later)
parameters.outside_cone: the special cannot be activated on that step; the card says why (Alex: sounds good)
parameters.aim_marker: dragging a step's aim marker moves that step's target (Alex: sounds good)
parameters.moving_target: a unit target FOLLOWS the unit; the release point is picked at resolve (record target-follows-unit)
parameters.lead: proposed: lead the followed unit by its velocity at the release x the fall time
parameters.target_leaves_cone: OPEN (record outside-cone-release): hold or poor_shot, data/sim/bombs.json outside_cone_mode

applied_to: scripts/ui/ui_target.gd, target_marks.gd, target_art.gd (the selection and its marks)
scripts/ui/motion_planner.gd, motion_planner_panel.gd (Drop takes the target onto the step)
scripts/sim/envelope.gd, world.gd, bombs.gd (the step's target, followed at resolve)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'For bombs, I expected area of effect as well. This implies each step might have a target which is either a unit or point. But this is only for specials. Let's look at our options here. Maybe a targeting selection is the right call. Specials use the current selection to set their target.' And: 'For selection, does this imply we have both a player unit and enemy unit selection?' Then: 'For targeting what I was actually thinking is when you have a friendly unit selected, you can also select either an enemy unit or a point on the map. The only thing it does is show on the side view and it is the target that the special will use if activated. Non-specials don't need targets because they autofire.' On no target: 'No target set means you can't activate special.' On the details: 'The special is active and targeted for the step. 1 - fine for now. Right click drag is ackwards so we will change later. 2 - not sure if meaningful across multiple steps. In theory a unit could have two targets for different specials across two steps. 3/4 sounds good.' Still open: how the area of effect is drawn (a board); On moving targets: 'Targeting a moving unit like a tank should follow the unit. We need to pick the release point for bombs and things dynamically.' Then: 'That means it might leave the cone and completely not fire.' Then: 'Or just be a bad shot.'

decisions.question: What does a special's target mean when the target is a unit that moves?

decisions.chosen: a unit target follows the unit: the sim resolves the release against where the unit goes, and the release point is picked dynamically; a point target is fixed

parameters.unit_target: stored on the step as {unit: id}; at resolve the aim is a function of the release moment (World._resolve_followed_drops, Bombs.plan_drop_moving)
parameters.preview: the planning aim of a unit target sits on the unit's SHOWN position; no projection of an enemy's motion is drawn or read (PROPOSED)
parameters.lead: PROPOSED by Track T, not Alex's: the unit's position at the release moment led by its velocity then times the fall time of a bomb released then (Bombs.followed_aim), so the stick lands where the unit is projected to be
parameters.release_moment: the moment of the step with the smallest release error for that moving aim (Bombs.best_release_moving)
parameters.unseen: PROPOSED: a followed unit that is out of the player side's sight at the release is still followed (the sim has no fog rule); a question for Alex

applied_to: tested in scripts/tests/test_bomb_target.gd with a test-only moving ground unit

decisions.question: What happens when a drop's target is outside its step's cone at release (a followed unit that leaves the cone during the resolve, or a step moved after the drop was set)?
options: hold: nothing is released and no bombs are spent
poor_shot: the stick is released at the cone's nearest point to the target, with the rim's accuracy or worse, and the bombs are spent
decisions.chosen: fire a poorer shot rather than hold it -- for bombs whose target leaves the cone and for guns whose target drops out of sight before they fire; an engagement mode may come later, not now

parameters.switch: data/sim/bombs.json outside_cone_mode -> poor_shot (decided; was hold while open); data/sim/guns.json gun_unspotted_mode -> poor_shot (the guns' twin, new)
parameters.poor_shot_floor: 0.15, PROPOSED: the least accuracy of a poor shot (rim accuracy / how far outside the cone, never below this)
parameters.planning_rule: stands either way (Alex): a special cannot be activated on a step whose cone does not hold the target; the card says why. The same for a gun: a target nobody sees or out of reach cannot be switched on
parameters.wording: PROPOSED: the card and the map say 'will not release: target outside the cone' under hold and 'poor shot: target outside the cone' under poor_shot (data/ui/ui.json bombs.text); a gun's fire already set whose target is not spotted or out of reach says 'poor shot: target is not spotted' (guns.text.poor_*, step_tag_poor) under poor_shot and 'will not fire: ...' under hold
parameters.gun_poor_shot: PROPOSED by Track CA: a salvo whose target is no longer spotted, or is out of reach (range, too close, off the coastal strip), when it fires IS fired and the reload spent: aimed at where the target was last spotted (its place at the last moment of the turn the side saw it, else the place it was shown at when the fire was set, else its place at the start of the turn; a point is where it is), no lead; pulled back along the line from the ship to the edge of the reach (range_max_m, range_min_m, the coastal strip) when that is outside it; each shell's scatter x poor_shot_factor 2.0 (data/sim/guns.json) and never under poor_shot_min_sigma_m 50 m; a poor shot is not a bracketing salvo. A reloading gun, a target already down, a friend and a missing target still hold
parameters.event: shell_fire with poor_shot: true, poor_why (unspotted | out_of_range | too_close | inland), known [x, y] and clamped; a held salvo is still a gun_hold

applied_to: data/sim/bombs.json outside_cone_mode: poor_shot (citing this decision); data/sim/guns.json gun_unspotted_mode: poor_shot, specials.main_guns.poor_shot_factor, poor_shot_min_sigma_m

decisions.question: What units come next?
decisions.chosen: mixed warfare, each mission with only a few elements: a big ship off the coast, tanks that move inland and spot anti-aircraft batteries for the ship's guns so airstrikes can go in; airstrikes that clear artillery so warships can engage supply boats; a small airfield where planes land to repair and rearm; trains as targets; observation balloons that tell the enemy where you are; mobile artillery that follows tanks and adds firepower without taking direct fire

parameters.mission_size: only a few elements per mission
parameters.capture_airfield: a mission objective: capture an airfield intact with tanks (so it could be based from); the basing itself is not simulated (Alex: 'as mission objective, don't need to sim that part')
parameters.ground_scale: ground objectives just start closer; engagement ranges are not settled yet (Alex: 'I am not sure what engagement ranges make sense yet')
parameters.shared_spotting: yes: any friendly unit's sight counts for every gun of its side; long-range guns need a spotted target
parameters.big_guns_as_specials: yes: a warship's main guns and artillery are specials, fired by hand with a long reload, aimed with the target selection
parameters.warship: not a full battleship: something smaller that operates more independently
parameters.sea_guns: range-limited: they reach the coast, not inland; a target's location can be unknown and must be found
parameters.role_vs_mission: a unit's role is what it can do; a mission picks a few units and the limits make the puzzle (no airbase, no planes; a mobile target needs spotters)
parameters.goal: a small set of missions that are fun tactics games; tie them together later; find the fun first
mission_ideas_alex: capture and hold a bridge at the far end of ship range, so shots need to be really on point
clear mobile AA units and their escorts to enable a bombing run on a military complex
repel a bombing run with mobile AA and a spotter plane
capture key tech and evacuate through enemy territory
rescue a downed pilot and his spy footage (close to 'capture the tech and evac')
parameters.first_mission: hold the bridge at the far end of ship range: it exercises more dynamic gameplay than we have now (Alex's pick)

decisions.notes: Alex: 'Let's plan some more units. I love the idea of mixed warfare. You have a huge ship parked off the coast but you need tanks to move inland to spot the aa batteries for the ship. Once it gets those to clear for airstrikes. Or you need airstrikes to clear artillery so the warships can engage the supply boats. Airplanes could land at a little airfield to repair and rearm. A train is a perfect target. Observation balloons could let the enemy know where you are. Mobile artillery could follow tanks to provide more firepower without taking direct fire.' Then: 'Each mission would only have a few elements'. Then: 'Capturing an airfield intact with tanks might make you able to base there (as mission objective, don't need to sim that part.' Answers to the four questions: '1. Ground objectives can just start closer. I am not sure what engagement ranges make sense yet. 2. Yes 3 yes 4 not a full battleship, something smaller that would operate more independently'. Then: '1. The sea guns have a range limit. You can attack coast not inland. Also the target location can be undetermined and needs to be found. But wait, we are mixing role and mission. A mission can always have limited units. No airbase? No planes. Mobile target? Needs spotters. We need to think through some fun mission ideas. Let's think through some historical tactics and how they might apply. For now our goal is a small set of missions that are fun tactics games. We can tie them together later. Find the fun first! Capture and hold a bridge, but you are at the far end of ship range so your shots need to be really on point to hit. Clear mobile Aa units and their escorts to enable a bombing run of a military complex. Rapel a bombing run with mobile aa and a spotter plane. Capture key tech and evac through enemy territory.' Then: 'Rescue a downed pilot and his spy footage' -- 'That was another idea but sounds similar to one you suggested. I like #1 the most, it lets us exercise more dynamic gameplay then we have now.'

decisions.question: Can tank guns damage a bridge?
decisions.chosen: tank guns can damage a bridge, but it should take a lot: a tank would have to sit there and shell it for a while, exposing itself

parameters.health: 14 pips (data/units/bridge.json, was 10), PROPOSED by Track CA: Alex gave the direction ('it should take a lot'), not the number. MEASURED with the real combat (scripts/test_support/bridge_tuning.gd): one tank's turret gun, stationary inside its 350 m range, takes 0.73 pips a turn, so 14 pips is a median of 20 turns of one tank firing steadily (10th to 90th percentile 13 to 23; the old 10 pips was 14 [10..17]). The lead's proposed target was about 15 to 20 turns
parameters.bombs: no single stick can drop it (the most a stick of 4 does is 12): a bomber on the ideal release needs 2.1 sticks from the low band, 3.4 from medium, 8.9 from high (3 drops in a load)
parameters.shells: a fresh direct salvo cannot (the most in 300 to 400 seeds: 13 pips at 600 m and at 1200 m, 7 at 3000 m); one ranged in for the full 20 s does it 35 percent of the time at 1200 m (1 percent at 3000 m), with a salvo already on the target 81 percent (7 percent at 3000 m), with two 99 percent (43 percent at 3000 m). Only 25 pips or more would be proof against a fully ranged salvo (6 shells x 4 pips is 24), and that is 34 turns for a tank: PROPOSED against, listed here so Alex can say

applied_to: scripts/tests/test_tank.gd (a tank's gun brings a bridge down: 8 seeds, none under 8 turns, about 20 on average), scripts/tests/test_water_units.gd (bombs: 3 direct leave 5 pips, the 5th destroys it), scripts/tests/test_cruiser.gd (a fresh direct salvo cannot one-shot it)

decisions.question: How does a forest fire work: what starts it, how it spreads and stops, what it does to units, what its smoke does to sight, what is left, how it looks, where it is tried first?
decisions.board: none for the rules (said in chat, on the lead's seven proposals); the look of a burning grove and a burnt-out tree: a board to come, after the mechanic is built with a stand-in
options: 1 ignition: bomb hits, shell hits and ground crashes; each tree within the blast catches at 50%
2 spread: once a turn each burning tree may light each tree within 30 m, 40% when canopies touch falling to 0 at 30 m; a tree burns 3 turns, then is burnt out
3 damage: ground and sea units within 25 m of a burning tree, 10% a turn to lose 1 pip; planes untouched
4 smoke and sight: a cover (seen only from close, like woods), b sight lines (smoke hides what is behind it; needs line of sight on), c aim (shots through smoke hit less often); the lead recommends a
5 a burnt-out tree takes its woods cover with it
6 the look: today's W1 smoke as a stand-in, a column per burning tree, then a board of 3-4 options for a burning grove and a burnt-out tree
7 tried first in Suppress, plus a sandbox switch
decisions.chosen: a forest fire is smoke coming from the trees, no flame; it is started by bomb hits, shell hits and ground crashes (each tree within the blast catches at 50%), spreads tree to tree by distance once a turn (40% when canopies touch, falling to 0 at 30 m), and a tree burns 3 turns, then burns down to its trunk; ground and sea units near a burning tree may lose 1 pip, 10% a turn fading with distance to 0 at 25 m; a burnt-out tree gives no woods cover; built first with W1 smoke as the stand-in look, then a board for the burning grove and the burnt-out trunk; tried first in Suppress; its smoke makes things harder to see (option a, refined): a ground or sea unit inside the smoke stays VISIBLE but cannot be TRACKED -- it cannot be taken as a unit target that follows it, and a special aimed at it (a bomb, the cruiser's guns) goes to the last place it was seen outside the smoke

parameters.smoke_only: burning trees draw smoke and no flame (consistent with decision fire-colour: 'No fire for now. Just smoke.')
parameters.ignite.radius: the event's blast_m for bombs and shells; PROPOSED for a crash, which has no blast: 20 m
parameters.spread.distance: PROPOSED: measured canopy edge to canopy edge, 40% at 0 m (or overlapping) falling linearly to 0 at 30 m
parameters.after: the tree burns down to its trunk (Alex: 'lets burn down to the trunks?'; the trunk's look comes from the board)
parameters.damage.fade: Alex: 'fade the change with distance as well'; PROPOSED: linear from 10% at a burning tree's canopy edge to 0 at 25 m, the trees combined as 1 - product(1 - p) and at most 1 pip a unit a turn, at the unit's closest approach in the turn
parameters.damage.who: ground and sea units; planes untouched
parameters.cover_after_burn: a burnt-out tree gives no woods cover; PROPOSED: the woods density at a point is scaled by the share of the trees within 20 m that are not burnt out
parameters.smoke_sight: a, refined (Alex: 'a', then '1 visible but untrackable and 2 last place you saw it'): smoke does not hide a unit (fog, the enemy AI's knowledge and woods cover are unchanged by it); it denies tracking: fire control (the cruiser's guns) does not count a target in smoke as spotted, so they fire the poorer shot at its last tracked place (decision outside-cone-release); a bomb following a unit that is in smoke at the release aims at the last place it was tracked; PROPOSED: ground and sea units, mobile and static, not planes; a click on an enemy in smoke sets a point target, not a unit target; leaving the smoke makes it trackable again
parameters.smoke.reach_m: PROPOSED: inside the smoke = within 20 m of a burning tree's canopy edge
parameters.look: W1 smoke (decision damage-smoke) as a stand-in column per burning tree; then a board for the burning grove and the burnt-out trunk

applied_to: to be built (track 'Forest fire', docs/status.md): data/sim/fire.json and scripts/sim/fire*.gd, the World's resolve and its net state, the effects layer's smoke per burning tree, the map's burnt trunks, Suppress
decisions.notes: Alex: 'I want to build a forest fire mechanic.' Then: 'I am thinking that the fire is actually just smoke coming from the trees. It spreads from tree to tree based on distance. It can inflict damage to nearby units with low power and low chance.' Then: 'It should generate smoke which makes it harder to see.' On the lead's seven proposals: '1 - yes 2 - yes 3 - lets fade the change with distance as well 4 - this is deeper then I was thinking. tell me more about this decision in a second. 5 - yes, lets burn down to the trunks? 6 - that is what I wanted 7 - suppress sounds good'. On the lead's explanation of question 4 (a cover, b sight lines, c aim): 'a - but confirm what the implication of this is.  the player might be able to visually see the unit on screen but won't be able to target it directly in a way that tracks it if it moves?' The lead explained that woods cover hides the marker entirely, that bombs today keep following a hidden target, and asked: hidden or visible but not trackable; a bomb's target lost in smoke aimed at its last-seen place? Alex: '1 visible but untrackable and 2 last place you saw it'. The numbers are starting values for a playtest (decision balance-uncalibrated); every detail marked PROPOSED is the lead's.
